clue.text: Feeling some regret about the church's decoration

indicators.note: about means one piece is placed around the other here

parts.note: ruing is feeling regret
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone feels a pang of remorse over how the church has been decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feeling some regret' looks like the definition, but the definition is 'decoration': ruching is gathered or pleated fabric used as trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruching is pleated or gathered fabric sewn on as ornamental trim, a kind of decoration.

clue.text: State the case for the most prosperous

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, a US state
a chest is a box or case

explanation.surface: Someone argues on behalf of the wealthiest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State the case' reads as 'argue', but it is a state and a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Richest means wealthiest, having the greatest prosperity.

clue.text: A dog may be about — or a soldier

parts.note: c, circa, means about
taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A dog might be loitering nearby, or there's a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh herding dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a breed of small Welsh herding dog.

clue.text: Picture, say, a great way to get a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say
the M1 is Britain's great motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Imagine a great method of getting a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get a rise' turns EG + A + MI upwards. The M1 is the main motorway from London to the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: It's good to pay attention and so look bright!

parts.note: to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Advice that attentiveness pays off and makes you look sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: To glisten is to shine or sparkle with reflected light.

clue.text: Tear after a dog, being up-to-date

indicators.note: after places the tear piece behind the dog piece in the answer

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: An image of someone ripping something after chasing a dog, while staying modern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' is the noun meaning a rip, not crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Current affairs are present-day matters, so current means contemporary or modern.

clue.text: Mean to cheat over record

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to con is to swindle or cheat
a note is a written record

explanation.surface: A nasty plan to swindle someone and falsify the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like the adjective for nasty, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To connote is to imply or signify, as a word suggests a sense beyond its literal one.

clue.text: All-round protection for a receiver of jewellery?

explanation.surface: A security perimeter set up around a fence dealing in stolen gems.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is someone who receives stolen goods, so a fence for a stolen ring is a 'ring fence'.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective barrier enclosing something on every side; and, punningly, a handler of a stolen band of gold.

clue.text: Dash to join up and work in most suitable sphere

indicators.note: in places the work piece inside the sphere piece

parts.note: being in one's element is being in the most suitable sphere
op, opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Rushing off to enlist and finding the job that suits you best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join up' looks like enlisting, but here it means marry.
explanation.definitionFit: An elopement is a secret runaway to marry, a dash to be wed.

clue.text: Some people just can't rest — lend them support

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken

parts.words: people just can't rest — lend them

explanation.surface: Some restless people need propping up.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt out across 'can't rest — lend'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework used to hold up a tabletop, a support.

clue.text: People going by private transport are in the pink

indicators.note: going by means travelling alongside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: a car is a private means of transport
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Motorists, it says, are in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the pink' looks like an idiom for healthy, but the pink is a flower family, and the carnation is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnations belong to the genus Dianthus, whose members are commonly called pinks.

clue.text: Such a trap can make one so mad!

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters going wild and rearranging

explanation.surface: An exclamation that being caught in some trap could drive a person crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges ONE and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A running loop of rope used to catch animals is a snare or trap.

clue.text: Obvious point with which a few create an impression

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
VI is the Roman numeral six, a few
to dent is to make an impression in a surface

explanation.surface: A writer's pointed remark that a handful of people can make their mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points (N, S, E, W) and Roman numerals are standard crossword sources of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plain to see, clear and apparent.

clue.text: Far from fresh buffet, and that's unusual

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad, far from fresh
to buffet is to strike or beat

explanation.surface: A stale buffet meal is described as odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a food spread, but it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat means unconventional or quirky, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: To make cuts without hesitation shows open-mindedness

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the cutting word goes around the hesitation

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a boil
er is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Cutting decisively, without dithering, is said to reveal a liberal mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, so the cutting word goes around the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is willingness to accept differing views, a broad and accepting attitude.

clue.text: Complaining of incorrect alignment

indicators.note: incorrect suggests the letters are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: Grumbling about bad wheel alignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrect' rearranges ALIGNMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamenting is expressing grief or grievance, mourning or bewailing.

clue.text: Whip off flimsy candle that's no longer in vogue

definitions.text: candle that's no longer in vogue

parts.note: to whip off is to dash or rush away
light means insubstantial or flimsy

explanation.surface: Snatch away a flimsy, old-fashioned candle.
explanation.walkthrough: A rushlight was a cheap candle made from a rush dipped in tallow, long obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushlight is an old type of cheap taper made from a dipped rush stem.

clue.text: Egghead occupying delightful young relative

indicators.note: occupying means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: nice means pleasant or delightful
the head, or first letter, of egg is E

explanation.surface: An intellectual is lodged with a charming youngster in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like an intellectual but is the first letter of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a brother's or sister's daughter, a younger family member.

clue.text: Hair-restorers concocted by doctor in a Greek island

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the island

parts.note: Cos, or Kos, is a Greek island in the Dodecanese
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A hair-growth remedy invented by a physician on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair-restorers' suggests baldness cures, but combs merely restore order to hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A comb tidies tangled hair, putting it back in order, which is the cryptic sense of restoring it.

clue.text: Company settling claim found amusing

indicators.note: settling suggests letters being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm resolving an insurance claim thought it funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settling' rearranges CLAIM into MICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Comical means funny, causing laughter.

clue.text: Arranged a merger, having carefully read about the backing etc

indicators.note: about means the reading word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to con is to study carefully, so conned means having read carefully

indicators.note: backing means the word etc is read backwards

explanation.surface: A deal-maker merged two firms after studying the supporting paperwork closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'etc' looks like part of the surface's list, but it is the fodder that 'the backing' turns round. To con is an old verb meaning to study or learn, so 'having carefully read' gives the reading word.
explanation.definitionFit: To have connected two things is to have joined or linked them, as a merger does.

clue.text: Gossip with many a mad character

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
the Mad Hatter is a character in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Gossiping with many eccentric people.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter is idle talk, the gist of gossip.

clue.text: Taking rest in a break and getting worse-tempered

indicators.note: break means the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone resting during a break and getting grumpier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges REST IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nastier means more unpleasant or ill-natured.

clue.text: A drop of French perfume

parts.note: de is French for of
a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: A droplet of French perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A drop of French perfume' reads as a dab of scent; the definition is just 'A drop'.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a downward slope or fall.

clue.text: Sort of brown paper freely available in a mall

indicators.note: freely suggests letters loosely rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Brown wrapping paper can be bought easily in a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely available' rearranges IN A MALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Manilla paper is a strong buff-coloured paper originally made from Manila hemp, used for envelopes.

clue.text: An ocean-going vessel must accommodate wide tastes

indicators.note: accommodate means the ship holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: SS, steamship, prefixes a ship's name
ample means large or wide

explanation.surface: A cruise liner should cater for broad preferences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tastes' looks like preferences, but it is small portions tried.
explanation.definitionFit: Samples are small trial portions, just as tastes are little tries of food.

clue.text: Retirement will not change her

indicators.note: retirement, read as going backwards, leaves the word the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman unaltered by going into retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' means going back: the answer reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address to a woman.

clue.text: The novice has a place in Tibet

parts.note: L, a learner, is a novice

explanation.surface: A beginner has a location in Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital city of Tibet.

clue.text: Stick a note on some fish

parts.note: C is a musical note
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An instruction to attach a label to some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to adhere or hold fast, as to stick.

clue.text: Poor trader hit badly

indicators.note: badly indicates the letters being knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: A merchant has been struck hard and is now in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TRADER HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something third-rate is inferior, of low quality.

clue.text: Landing craft?

parts.note: a vessel that ferries cargo from ship to shore, landing goods; also a craft (skill) of making things less heavy

explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships and land their cargo ashore.

clue.text: Defence force section

parts.note: to ram is to force, drive hard
a part is a section

explanation.surface: A section of the defence force, as in a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or embankment around a fort.
